title: Foundations of the Republic
subject: Polity
objectives: Sequence key milestones in the making of the Constitution.
Explain the Objectives Resolution's relationship to the Preamble.
Apply constitutional values to a governance scenario.

lessons.title: A Constitution made by its people

sections.heading: The Constituent Assembly
sections.body: The Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946. It worked through committees, debate and drafting. The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

sections.heading: Why 26 January?
sections.body: The date honoured the Purna Swaraj declaration of 26 January 1930. Adoption and commencement are distinct events: the text was adopted in November 1949, while the republic began in January 1950.

sections.heading: The Drafting Committee
sections.body: The Drafting Committee, chaired by Dr B. R. Ambedkar, prepared a draft for the Assembly to consider. Constitution-making was a collective process involving the Assembly and its committees.

keyTakeaways: The Drafting Committee was chaired by B. R. Ambedkar.

lessons.title: From political resolve to constitutional purpose

sections.heading: Nehru's resolution
sections.body: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946. The Assembly adopted it on 22 January 1947. It expressed the political ideals that were to guide constitution-making.

sections.heading: A bridge to the Preamble
sections.body: The Resolution is a major source of the Preamble's philosophy. The Preamble gives concise expression to constitutional purposes, but the two are not interchangeable documents.

keyTakeaways: Moved on 13 December 1946 and adopted on 22 January 1947.
It informed the philosophy later expressed in the Preamble.

lessons.title: Reading the Preamble as a compass

sections.heading: The constitutional promise
sections.body: The Preamble identifies India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic and commits the Constitution to justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. It helps readers understand the Constitution's broad purposes.

sections.heading: Interpretive role
sections.body: The Preamble is part of the Constitution and can assist constitutional interpretation. It is not an independent source of power and cannot override clear constitutional provisions.

keyTakeaways: The Preamble states constitutional ideals and objectives.
It guides interpretation but does not independently confer power.

activities.title: Recall the milestones
activities.prompt: Without looking back, state the dates on which the Constitution was adopted and came into force.
activities.hint: Adoption was in November; commencement was on Republic Day.
activities.answer: Adopted on 26 November 1949; came into force on 26 January 1950.
activities.explanation: The Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949. It came into force on 26 January 1950, the date observed as Republic Day.

activities.title: The guiding resolution
activities.prompt: Who moved the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly?
activities.hint: He later became India's first Prime Minister.
activities.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru moved it on 13 December 1946; the Assembly adopted it on 22 January 1947.

activities.title: Preamble: fact or inference?
activities.prompt: Which statement best describes the Preamble's legal role?
activities.hint: Look for the distinction between interpretation and independent power.
statements: It can assist interpretation of ambiguous provisions.
activities.explanation: The Preamble guides interpretation but is not an independent source of governmental power.

activities.title: Assertion and reason
activities.prompt: Assertion: The Preamble can help courts interpret constitutional provisions. Reason: It expresses the broad objectives and values of the Constitution.
activities.hint: Test each statement, then test whether the reason explains the assertion.

options.text: Both are true, and the reason explains the assertion
Both are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion
Assertion is true, reason is false
Assertion is false, reason is true

activities.explanation: The Preamble states the constitutional purposes that help orient interpretation, so the reason supports the assertion.

activities.title: Adoption vs commencement
activities.prompt: In two concise points, distinguish adoption of the Constitution from its commencement.
activities.hint: Give the date for each and explain what changed on each date.
activities.answer: Adopted on 26 November 1949; came into force on 26 January 1950, when India became a republic under it.
activities.modelAnswer: Adoption (26 November 1949) was the Assembly's approval of the text. Commencement (26 January 1950) brought the Constitution into force and marked the beginning of the republic.
activities.explanation: Keeping the two dates separate prevents a common factual error in polity questions.

activities.title: Values in administration
activities.caseStudy: A district office introduces an online-only application process. Residents in remote areas with poor connectivity cannot access the service. The administration has budget for a limited number of assisted service points.
activities.prompt: Identify the constitutional values at stake and recommend one practical, inclusive response.
activities.hint: Consider equality of access, dignity, and a remedy that keeps the service usable.
activities.answer: Recognize equality and dignity concerns; add assisted access points, maintain an offline route, and review access data.
activities.modelAnswer: The process raises equality and dignity concerns because a formally uniform digital channel excludes residents facing connectivity barriers. The district should establish assisted service points and retain an offline route, prioritizing underserved areas and reviewing uptake to improve access.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the measure addresses exclusion

activities.explanation: Good application answers connect a constitutional value to a concrete administrative remedy and show why it reduces exclusion.

activities.title: Mains practice: constitutional values
activities.prompt: The Preamble is both a statement of constitutional philosophy and an aid to interpretation. Discuss in about 150 words.
activities.hint: Define its purpose, explain its interpretive role, and state one legal limit.
activities.answer: A strong answer distinguishes constitutional philosophy from enforceable powers, explains interpretive use, and notes that the Preamble cannot override explicit provisions.
activities.modelAnswer: The Preamble expresses the Constitution's foundational commitments, including justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. It offers a concise account of the objectives that animate the constitutional scheme. Courts may use it as an interpretive aid, particularly where a provision admits more than one reading, because it helps identify the direction of the constitutional design. Its role nevertheless has limits: it is not an independent source of governmental power or a substitute for operative provisions, and it cannot override clear constitutional text. The Preamble is therefore best understood as a compass for reading the Constitution within, rather than apart from, its legal structure.
activities.explanation: Use the rubric to self-assess after writing. The model answer is a guide, not the only valid formulation.

activities.title: Quick review: Objectives Resolution
activities.prompt: Who moved the Objectives Resolution, and on what date was it adopted?
activities.hint: The mover became the first Prime Minister; adoption was in January 1947.
activities.answer: Jawaharlal Nehru moved it; it was adopted on 22 January 1947.
activities.explanation: It was moved on 13 December 1946 and adopted on 22 January 1947.

activities.title: Boss encounter: the republic's foundations
activities.prompt: A learner claims the Constitution was adopted on Republic Day and that the Preamble itself grants Parliament power to act. Identify both errors and correct them.
activities.hint: Separate adoption from commencement, then distinguish an interpretive guide from a source of power.

options.text: Adopted 26 Nov 1949; commenced 26 Jan 1950. Preamble guides interpretation, not an independent source of power.
Adopted 26 Jan 1950; the Preamble is a source of power.

activities.explanation: A strong response catches both the date confusion and the Preamble's limited legal function.
